purpose: Identify the phase and allocation lifetime responsible for the CMIX high-water mark, then authorize only a probability-identical memory child unless evidence proves that semantics must change.
measurement_rules: Record all memory quantities in bytes. Preserve the raw procfs kB values separately when procfs is the source.
Identify every process by PID plus /proc start ticks so PID reuse cannot alter tree membership.
Sample process-tree RSS continuously and retain every per-process VmHWM observed before process exit.
When available, place the complete invocation in a dedicated cgroup-v2 subtree and retain memory.current, memory.peak, memory.events, and memory.stat.
At phase boundaries, capture smaps_rollup and a normalized mapping inventory for every live process.
Record logical and allocated scratch bytes separately.
A lower sampled RSS never overrides a larger per-process VmHWM or cgroup memory.peak.
A missing short-lived process, unreadable procfs record, dropped sample, clock regression, or observer failure makes the affected peak interval incomplete.
The observer may terminate a future run at a hard limit but must never mutate codec state, files, affinity, allocation policy, or process priority.
phase_marker_rules: Source markers may identify phase transitions but must not report memory values as authority.
Each marker carries a monotonic timestamp, process identity, sequence number, phase name, event kind, and canonical payload hash.
Markers must be emitted before the first phase operation and after the last phase operation.
Unexpected, duplicated, skipped, or reordered markers invalidate phase attribution but do not erase independently observed memory evidence.
Instrumentation overhead must be measured against an observer-only K control on the same bounded scope.
allocation_attribution_rules: Name a dominant allocation only when mapping, allocator, or source evidence binds its owner and lifetime to the high-water interval.
Do not infer reclaimability from virtual size alone.
Do not classify file-backed or shared pages as uncounted merely because they are not anonymous heap.
For each proposed reduction, identify whether it changes model capacity, probability arithmetic, context retention, preprocessing, archive construction, or decoder-visible state.
Sum reclaimable bytes only for allocations whose lifetimes overlap at the authoritative peak.
Do not add mutually exclusive counterfactual reductions.
A probability-identical proposal must explain why allocation order, initialization, table contents, state cadence, and arithmetic results remain unchanged.

probability_identity_required.rule: If any probability-, state-, payload-, archive-, or inverse-affecting value changes, the memory child is a new compression candidate and restarts the archive ladder.

diagnostic_population.first_scope: smallest scope that reproduces model initialization and all suspected high-water allocation lifetimes

attribution_pass: Every phase has ordered begin and end evidence or an explicit terminal exception.
The authoritative peak interval has complete process-tree and per-process evidence.
Dominant allocation identities cover enough simultaneously resident bytes to explain the measured excess.
Reclaimable lower bounds are based on overlapping lifetimes rather than summed maxima.
The receipt names one exact memory-child hypothesis or concludes that only semantics-changing reductions remain.
memory_child_authorization: The proposed probability-identical reduction lower bound exceeds 1,508,229,120 bytes using the current Arm B lower-bound peak, or is recomputed upward from the terminal peak.
The proposal targets at most one coherent allocation-lifetime mechanism.
The source revision, patch digest, build recipe, corpus, parameters, coder, and comparison parent are frozen before compilation.
One correction-only implementation successor is permitted for implementation failure; no flag sweep is permitted.

qualification_sequence: Run attribution diagnostically after Arm B terminalizes and the exclusive lease is released.
Freeze one memory-child realization from the dominant overlapping allocation evidence.
At 250KB, require probability, payload, state, and inverse identity plus observer integrity.
At 1MB, require repeat identity and a measured memory reduction consistent with the attributed allocation lifetime.
At the smallest scope reproducing peak allocation lifetimes, require the engineering target with both instrumented and observer-only comparisons.
Run one uninstrumented guarded qualification from a clean build; diagnostic instrumentation cannot confer resource authority.
Authorize a new full-1G parent qualification only after the uninstrumented evidence is below 9,216,000,000 bytes with sufficient phase-independent margin.
At full 1G, require exact archive and inverse identity against the external parent plus a terminal resource-guard receipt.

terminal_branches.probability_identical_reduction_reaches_: Promote the exact memory-safe parent through the archive ladder.
terminal_branches.probability_identical_reduction_only_cro: Do not run full 1G; seek one correction-only lifetime reduction that reaches the engineering target.
terminal_branches.only_semantics_changing_reduction_availa: Version a new parent candidate and restart compression, inverse, determinism, package, and transfer gates.
terminal_branches.attribution_incomplete: Preserve the receipt and authorize one correction-only observer or marker successor.
terminal_branches.reduction_subscale: Retire the memory-child hypothesis; do not combine non-overlapping or mutually exclusive estimates.
